title: Decoded #9: Build a Test Calendar, Not a Content Calendar
hook: A content calendar schedules output. A test calendar schedules learning.
caption:
Most 2027 plans landing this week answer one question: what will we post?

Very few answer the question that matters more: what will we know by March that we don't know now?

In Issue #7 of Decoded, Raj makes the case for a test calendar instead of a content calendar: one question per fortnight, a fixed test budget, the expected result written before launch, and India's 2027 festival and sale dates mapped to the reasons to buy worth testing. It includes a one-page template you can copy into your planning doc.

# Decoded · Issue #7 — 2027 creative planning: build a test calendar, not a content calendar
*Skeleton — Raj to write in full. ~1,500 words when finished. Sends in the quiet week between Christmas and New Year: keep it practical and short to read.*

**Opening (Monday, 9:40 a.m.):** Sam's agency sends the 2027 content calendar: 52 weeks, every festival, a theme per month. It answers "what will we post?" It never answers "what will we know by March that we don't know now?"

**Key takeaways (draft):**
1. A content calendar schedules output. A test calendar schedules learning.
2. Each fortnight should test one question: a hook, a buyer, a format or an offer. Not all four.
3. Festivals and sale days are fixed dates for testing reasons to buy, not just for greetings.

**Section 1 — Why content calendars fail performance teams.** They plan volume, not questions. Thirty ads on one theme are, to Meta, close to one ad (Issue #3).

**Section 2 — The test calendar, step by step.** (1) List the five questions you most need answered (e.g. "does a customer in the first frame beat the founder?"). (2) Give each a fortnight. (3) Decide the budget share for tests up front. (4) Write the expected result before launch. (5) Review on a fixed day; log the answer in Brand Memory.

**Section 3 — Mapping 2027's Indian calendar to tests.** January: harvest festivals and Republic Day sales — test urgency vs value. February–March: financial year-end budgets — test proof-led creative. Holi (22 March) and summer: test settings and seasonal moments. Festive season (Navratri from 30 Sep, Diwali on 29 Oct): plan tests in August, not October. Sale windows are estimates until platforms announce them.

**Section 4 — What Galvor saw in the data.** [DATA NEEDED: how often brands we work with launched tests with a written hypothesis vs without, and the difference in what was learned; anonymised.] Back with: give new ads time (~35% dearer early); never launch six look-alikes in three days (48% less).

**Section 5 — The shift for marketers and leaders: five moves.** (1) Replace "posts per month" with "questions answered per month". (2) One question per fortnight. (3) Protect a fixed test budget. (4) Plan festive tests eight weeks early. (5) Share the test calendar with finance (bridge to Issue #9).

**Template to include:** a one-page test calendar table (fortnight · question · attribute changed · expected result · budget share · owner · result).

**Next issue:** The learning loop — how to run a fortnightly creative cycle.
